chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a grave robber. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) grabbed him by his hair, struck him against the ground, then ordered the people to trample him with their feet. So they trampled him until he died.

key_terms.نَبَّاش: Grave robber (one who digs up graves to steal shrouds or valuables)

ai.seo_question: What was the specific punishment for a grave robber according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the severity of the hadd penalty for grave robbers (al-Nabbashin) in early Shia jurisprudence, where Imam Ali (peace be upon him) personally executed the offender by striking him to the ground before ordering the public to trample him until death. This method underscores the physical humiliation and finality of the punishment, reflecting the high value placed on preserving the sanctity of graves in the Islamic community. The incident serves as a key precedent for the application of capital punishment for this specific crime during the Rashidun period.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from someone else from our companions who said,

‘They came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with a grave robber man. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> grabbed him by his hair, and struck him down on the ground. Then he<sup>asws</sup> ordered the people that they should trample upon him with their feet. So he was trampled until he died’.
